 Korean skincare brand builds on online sellout, expanding into Costco stores as it targets North American consumers 
 Re:NK’s Cell to Cell® Cream / Courtesy of Coway 
 Re, the cosmetics brand operated by Coway's beauty subsidiary HILLABEE, has expanded its presence in the U.S. market with the launch of its flagship Cell to Cell Cream at Costco's brick-and-mortar stores.
 HILLABEE said on Nov. 2 that sales of the Cell to Cell Cream began at U.S. Costco stores on Nov. 1. The move follows the product's early sellout on Costco's U.S. online store in March, extending its distribution from e-commerce to physical retail.
 Last month, Re introduced its Celestial Collagen Cream through Costco's Beauty Table program, which showcases emerging beauty brands and products. The addition of Cell to Cell Cream further broadens the brand's offline product lineup and brings it to a wider range of local consumers.
 Cell to Cell Cream is an anti-aging skincare product designed to address multiple concerns, including skin elasticity, wrinkles and dryness. It features Re's proprietary cell science technology and contains 250,000 units of its REAL CELL ingredients derived from plants such as everlasting flower, Arabian myrrh and American prickly pear.
 According to the company, the technology was developed through joint research with the University of Bordeaux in France. It is designed to preserve the original structure of plant cells while incorporating active ingredients for delivery to the skin.
 The product also underwent a four-week clinical study involving 30 women aged 35 to 60. The company said the study showed improvements in key skin indicators, including hydration, skin density, wrinkles and elasticity.
 Re plans to use the Costco launch as a springboard to expand its product portfolio in the United States and strengthen its position in the premium skincare segment. The company aims to build on its online sales performance and increase its reach through major offline retail channels.
 HILLABEE also operates V&A Beauty, a cosmetics brand licensed by London's Victoria and Albert Museum; Olbit, a traditional herbal skincare brand; and health supplement brand HealthyGRO.
